subject: Post-call: Implementation brief & next steps — structured outputs, streaming, embeddings
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@evermed.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@evermed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Implementation brief & next steps — structured outputs, streaming, embeddings

Thanks again for carving out time today — really appreciate the clear signal around the use case. Quick recap from our side so everyone is aligned and we can move to a short technical deep-dive: 

Pain points you shared:
- Current doc summarization pipeline is inconsistent for multi-section clinical notes; downstream QA requires manual curation.
- Long-tail latency spikes during peak batch processing causing missed SLAs for clinicians.
- Need for structured, validated JSON outputs (discrete fields) to feed into your EHR ingest.

Goals we captured:
- 95%+ accuracy on key-field extraction for discharge summary fields (diagnoses, meds, follow-up instructions) vs. your labeled dataset.
- End-to-end P99 latency target for single-note inference <= 450ms when served in Dedicated capacity; target 200ms for streaming previews.
- Embedding-based similarity/rerank for retrieval of similar prior notes with top-5 recall > 0.88.

Product/Integration items we discussed:
- SDK integration: you prefer a lightweight Python SDK call that supports streaming token-by-token preview and final structured JSON validation.
- Function calling: we will expose a typed function signature that returns a JSON object matching your schema.
- Streaming + structured outputs: streaming will emit partial JSON segments (prefixed with events) and then a final validated payload.
- Embeddings/rerank: we recommended a 1536-d embedding with cosine similarity + a learned reranker for top-K precision.

Open technical clarifications we need from your team:
1) Typical average input length (tokens) and distribution (50th / 90th / 99th percentile).
2) QPS expected during peak (concurrent clinical workflows, approximate).
3) Which internal PII controls/audit logs are required beyond SOC2 (retention window, encryption-at-rest details).

Next steps and owners:
- Rajiv: please share a small sample set (10–20 deidentified notes) so our ML team can run an initial schema-compatibility check (requested by Tue, Aug 17).
- Dev (Dev Patel): prepare a short proposal for SDK changes and streaming contract by Wed, Aug 18.
- Kimberly: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive for Thu, Aug 19 — calendar invite to follow.

Attaching a draft mock-output-schema.json (very rough) so we can converge on field names.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Danielle Park <danielle.park@evermed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@evermed.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Implementation brief & next steps — structured outputs, streaming, embeddings

Kim — thanks for the clear write-up, this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Input lengths: typical discharge note ~ 400–800 tokens; 90th percentile ~ 1,400 tokens; we see occasional >3k tokens.
- Peak QPS: during morning rounds we expect up to 30 concurrent note generations and a background batch that processes ~120/hr.
- Compliance: SOC2 baseline in place; additional requirements — 7 year retention for audit logs, customer-managed KMS for keys is preferred, and we need request-level audit IDs surfaced to our SIEM.

We will upload 12 deidentified notes to the shared S3 link (s3://evermed-deid-samples) by EOD Tue. Rajiv will coordinate on the access and send the presigned links.

One more ask: can you confirm behavior when streaming partial JSON fails validation mid-stream (e.g., missing closing braces)? We'd prefer the stream include incremental validation events and a final "commit" event only after the output passes schema checks.

Thanks — Danielle

--
Danielle Park
Head of Product, Clinical Informatics | EverMed Health
danielle.park@evermed.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@evermed.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 16:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Implementation brief & next steps — structured outputs, streaming, embeddings

Thanks, Danielle — good details. Technical follow-ups from our infra/runtime perspective: 

- Streaming semantics: we can implement an "evented" stream where we send chunks of the inferred model output plus discrete validation events. Suggested pattern: 
  * data: partial-json-fragment
  * validation: {"path":"/medications","status":"ok"} or {"path":"/medications","status":"error","message":"type mismatch"}
  * commit: final-validated-payload (only emitted if schema passes)

- Failure modes: if a final commit fails validation we will emit a structured error with a deterministic error_code and include the full partial payload for debugging. We can also provide an automatic fallback to a non-streamed synchronous generation of the validated JSON as an option.

- Latency: with Dedicated capacity and the expected note sizes, we can target 200–300ms median and keep P99 under 600ms for full validated output; streaming previews for the first 200 tokens should arrive in <120ms. We'll validate with your 12 samples and report actuals.

- Embeddings/rerank: we recommend running an initial prototype with 1536-d open model embeddings inside Redwood Dedicated; for rerank we will supply a simple logistic reranker trained on your relevance labels. We need a small set of relevance-labeled pairs (100–300) to bootstrap.

Questions for EverMed: 
1) Does your EHR ingest expect strictly typed values (dates as ISO8601, medication names normalized) or will you accept string fields with downstream normalization?
2) Do you require opaque request IDs to be returned on each response for traceability?

I'll drop a short doc with the streaming contract and an SDK patch diff by Wed evening. Marcus — I'll loop you for perf testing and can we reserve a Dedicated slot for a two-week pilot (prefer Aug 24–Sep 6)?

- Dev

--
Dev Patel

- Marcus: please provision Dedicated pilot capacity Aug 24–Sep 6 and reserve 4 GPUs for the initial run (owner: Marcus Lin).
- Kimberly: schedule the technical deep-dive Thu, Aug 19, 10:00–11:00 PT (invite sent).

I've attached the mock-output-schema.json (very quick draft) and the EverMed system requirements PDF you shared — we'll iterate on field names during the deep-dive. If everyone is good, I'll convert these next steps into a mutual action plan in HubSpot after the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Kim
